ABU.note: Independent/exhibition club distinct from the APFA's Buffalo All-Americans (BFF); played Rochester and Buffalo All-Americans in 1920.

AKR.note: Won the first APFA championship in 1920; later known as the Akron Indians.

ARI.note: Founding APFA franchise (Chicago/Racine Cardinals); continuous lineage through St. Louis (1960-1987) to Arizona (1988-present).

ATN.note: Independent club that played Rochester and Buffalo in 1920.

BAL.note: Franchise relocated from Cleveland in 1996; not related to the original (AAFC/NFL) Baltimore Colts, code BCL.

BBA.note: All-America Football Conference team; Bisons in 1946, renamed Bills 1947-1949. Folded when the AAFC dissolved after 1949; unrelated corporate lineage to the modern Buffalo Bills (BUF).

BCL.note: Formerly the Miami Seahawks (AAFC, 1946), relocated to Baltimore 1947; joined the NFL in the 1950 AAFC merger and folded after that one NFL season. No direct lineage to the modern Indianapolis Colts (IND) or Baltimore Ravens (BAL).

BDA.note: AAFC team, separate from the NFL's Brooklyn Dodgers (BKN); merged into the AAFC New York Yankees for the 1949 season.

BFF.note: Later renamed Buffalo Bisons, then Buffalo Rangers; inactive in 1928.

BKN.note: Originally the Brooklyn Lions lineage continued as the Dodgers; renamed Brooklyn Tigers for its final 1944 season.

BRL.note: One-season NFL franchise, separate franchise history from the later Brooklyn Dodgers (BKN).

BUF.note: Original AFL franchise (1960), joined NFL in 1970 merger.

BYK.note: Became the New York Bulldogs/Yanks (NYY) in 1949; that lineage eventually became the Dallas Texans (DTX, 1952) and then the new Baltimore Colts (1953), ancestor of today's Indianapolis Colts (IND) — though the NFL treats the 1953 Colts as a new franchise.

CBD.note: Won NFL championships in 1922 and 1923; many players moved to the Cleveland Bulldogs (CIB) in 1924 before the Canton franchise returned in 1925-1926.

CCL.note: Official APFA-member season for the Celts (1-3 league record); a traveling team with no home games. Distinct 538/PFR code from CNC, which covers the team's 1920 non-league games.

CHB.note: Independent club that beat the Hammond Pros in 1920.

CHI.note: Founded as the Decatur Staleys (1920), became Chicago Staleys (1921), then Chicago Bears (1922-present).

CHL.note: Independent club beaten by the Decatur Staleys in 1920.

CIB.note: Played as Cleveland Indians most seasons and as the Cleveland Bulldogs in 1924, when (largely stocked with ex-Canton Bulldogs players) it won the NFL championship.

CLE.note: Founded in the AAFC (1946-1949), joined the NFL in the 1950 merger.

CLI.note: One-season revival of the Cleveland Indians name, separate franchise entry from the 1923-1927 Cleveland Indians/Bulldogs (CIB).

CLP.note: Independent club, played the Detroit Heralds in 1920; distinct from the Cleveland Tigers (CTI).

CNC.note: The Celts' 1920 non-league/independent schedule; the team's official 1921 APFA season is coded separately as CCL.

CRA.note: AAFC team; Rockets 1946-1948, renamed Hornets for its final 1949 season, then dissolved.

CRP.note: One-season wartime manpower-shortage merger of the Cardinals and Steelers, infamous for going winless (0-10); nicknamed the "Carpets." Both parent franchises (ARI, PIT) resumed independently in 1945.

CST.note: Independent Chicago club that played non-league exhibition games against the Cardinals and Staleys; not an APFA member.

CTI.note: Played as Cleveland Tigers in 1920 and Cleveland Indians in 1921 before going dormant; distinct franchise thread from the later Cleveland Indians/Bulldogs (CIB) and 1931 Cleveland Indians (CLI).

CWP.note: Independent club that played the Columbus Panhandles in 1920.

DAY.note: One of the APFA's founding members; sold and relocated to become the Brooklyn Dodgers (NFL) in 1930.

DET.note: Originated as the 1930 Portsmouth Spartans; became the Detroit Lions in 1934.

DTI.note: NFL/APFA franchise, unrelated to the MLB Detroit Tigers.

DTM.note: Independent club, tied the Detroit Heralds in 1920.

DTX.note: Continuation of the New York Yanks (NYY) lineage; folded mid-notoriety as the last NFL franchise to go fully defunct, with the league taking it over and later awarding a new Baltimore franchise (the 1953 Colts, ancestor of today's Indianapolis Colts) the following year.

DUL.note: Renamed Duluth Eskimos in 1926, famous for touring nationally behind star Ernie Nevers.

ELY.note: Independent club, tied the Columbus Panhandles in 1920.

FTP.note: Team associated with the Fort Porter Army post in Buffalo; played Rochester in 1920.

FYJ.note: Won the 1926 NFL championship; folded in 1931, and Bert Bell later used remnants of the franchise to help found the Philadelphia Eagles (PHI) in 1933.

GAR.note: Independent club, beat the Hammond Pros in 1920.

GUN.note: Joined the NFL mid-season 1934 as a replacement for the Cincinnati Reds.

HAM.note: Also known as the Hammond All-Stars/Bobcats; a traveling team with no home games in 1920.

IND.note: Founded 1953 in Baltimore (new franchise, not the original AAFC/NFL Baltimore Colts, BCL); relocated to Indianapolis in 1984.

KC.note: Founded as the Dallas Texans (AFL, 1960-1962), moved to Kansas City in 1963.

KCB.displayName: Kansas City Blues / Kansas City Cowboys

KEW.note: Independent club, lost to the Decatur Staleys in 1920.

LAB.note: A traveling team with no home games; not related to any later LA-area franchise.

LAC.note: Founding AFL franchise, originally in Los Angeles (1960) then San Diego (1961-2016) before returning to the LA area in 2017.

LAN.note: Independent club sponsored by the Oldsmobile automaker; played Detroit Heralds and Chicago Cardinals in 1920.

LAR.note: Founded 1936 in Cleveland (AFL), joined NFL 1937; moved to Los Angeles (1946-1994), St. Louis (1995-2015), then back to LA (2016-present).

LDA.note: AAFC franchise; folded when the AAFC dissolved after the 1949 season and was not one of the three teams absorbed into the NFL.

LOG.note: Independent club from Chicago's Logan Square neighborhood; lost to the Hammond Pros in 1920.

MCK.note: Independent club, lost to Buffalo All-Americans in 1920.

MNM.note: Independent club in 1920, the year before formally joining the APFA (see MNN).

MNN.note: Renamed Red Jackets for its final 1929-1930 seasons.

MSA.note: AAFC franchise that went bankrupt after one season; its assets became the Baltimore Colts (BCL) in 1947.

MUT.note: Independent club, played the Decatur Staleys and Chicago Cardinals in 1920.

NAA.note: AAFC franchise, distinct from the earlier NFL New York Yankees (NYA); absorbed the Brooklyn Dodgers (AAFC, BDA) roster for the 1949 season, then dissolved with the AAFC.

NE.note: Founding AFL franchise as the Boston Patriots (1960).

NG1.note: One-season APFA team coached by Charlie Brickley, also called the Brooklyn Giants in some contemporary advertising; no relation to the modern New York Giants (NYG), founded in 1925.

NYA.note: NFL franchise built around Red Grange; distinct from the later AAFC New York Yankees (NAA).

NYJ.note: Founding AFL franchise as the New York Titans (1960-1962), renamed Jets in 1963.

NYY.displayName: New York Bulldogs / New York Yanks
NYY.note: Continuation of the Boston Yanks (BYK); renamed Bulldogs (1949) then Yanks (1950-1951); its player contracts were dispersed to form the Dallas Texans (DTX) in 1952.

OAK.note: Founding AFL franchise in Oakland; this dataset labels the team OAK throughout its history, including 1982-1994 (Los Angeles) and 2020 (final Oakland season before the Las Vegas move).

OOR.note: Roster composed entirely of Native American players, coached by and starring Jim Thorpe; sponsored by the Oorang Dog Kennel company.

PIT.note: Known as the Pittsburgh Pirates until 1940.

PTB.note: Claimed the 1925 NFL title on the field but were controversially stripped of recognition by the league; relocated to Boston as the Bulldogs for their final 1929 season.

PTQ.note: Independent club, lost to the Canton Bulldogs in 1920.

PUL.note: Independent club from Chicago's Pullman neighborhood; lost to the Hammond Pros in 1920.

RAC.note: Renamed Tornadoes for its final 1926 season.

RCK.note: Independent club, lost to the Decatur Staleys in 1920.

RED.note: NFL franchise; unrelated to the MLB Cincinnati Reds. Replaced mid-1934 by the St. Louis Gunners (GUN).

RIC.note: Independent club, lost to the Canton Bulldogs in 1920.

RII.note: One of the APFA's founding members.

ROS.note: Independent club that played the Rochester Jeffersons three times in 1920.

SEN.note: NFL/APFA franchise, unrelated to the MLB Washington Senators.

SF.note: Founded in the AAFC (1946-1949), joined the NFL in the 1950 merger.

STG.note: One-season wartime manpower-shortage merger of the Eagles and Steelers, popularly nicknamed the Steagles. Both parent franchises (PHI, PIT) resumed independently in 1944.

STP.note: Independent club, lost the Rock Island Independents' 1920 season opener.

SYR.note: Independent club, lost to Rochester in 1920.

TEN.note: Founding AFL franchise as the Houston Oilers (1960); relocated to Tennessee in 1997, renamed Titans in 1999.

THO.note: Independent club that played some home games in Monmouth, IL; faced Rock Island and the Chicago Tigers in 1920.

TLM.note: The team's 1920 (independent-era) games; its later 1922-1923 APFA/NFL seasons are coded separately as TOL.

TOL.note: Official APFA/NFL member seasons for the Maroons; see also TLM for the team's 1920 games.

TON.note: One-season APFA franchise, distinct from the independent 1920 All-Tonawanda Lumberjacks (ATN).

UAP.note: Independent club, beat the Canton Bulldogs in 1920.

UTI.note: Independent club, played Rochester twice in 1920.

WBU.note: Independent club, lost to Buffalo All-Americans in 1920.

WGC.displayName: Washington Glee Club (New Haven Washington Glees)
WGC.note: Despite the name, based in New Haven, CT; tied the Canton Bulldogs (featuring Jim Thorpe) 0-0 in December 1920.

WHE.note: Independent club, lost to the Akron Pros in 1920.

WJA.note: Independent club tied to Washington & Jefferson College; lost to Rock Island in 1920.

WSH.note: Founded as the Boston Braves (1932), became Boston Redskins (1933), moved to Washington in 1937 as the Redskins; renamed Washington Football Team (2020-2021) then Commanders (2022-present).

ZAN.note: Independent club, played the Columbus Panhandles twice in 1920.
